scope.flow: backstop liquidation matching against posted orders outside divergence caps
scope.environment: perpetual/orderbook protocol with divergence caps, backstop liquidation, and admin-set divergence cap

statements.text: Bob has an open short position on ETH that is undercollateralized and eligible for backstop liquidation.
Alice submits a sell (ask) order at a price significantly above the max diverging ask price.
No opposing long orders exist in the book, so Alice's post-only order does not fill and revert with PostOnlyOrderWouldBeFilled().

The protocol lacks checks during order posting, allowing users to submit orders with prices far outside the divergence bounds; the matching loops break on bestAsk > maxAsk and bestBid < minBid, so the out-of-range order cannot be filled.
Admin or backstop liquidator calls backstopLiquidate.
backstopLiquidate reverts with ZeroOrder() due to the divergence check when the only available ask is outside the divergence cap.
The divergence cap is reduced via setDivergenceCap to a value lower than current orders' prices, so previously valid orders fall outside the new range.
Orders should only be placed when the order price is not outside the divergence ranges.
Orders falling outside the price ranges on both standard and backstop orderbooks should be forcefully closed so they do not remain outside the divergence range.

ambiguities: Report does not state whether Alice's posting is permissionless or requires authorization; no explicit anyone-can-call statement.
The ZeroOrder() revert is described as the outcome of backstopLiquidate; whether it is the direct violation witness or a downstream consequence is not fully separated in prose.
Timing/order relation between Alice's posting and the liquidator's call is described as requiring careful timing but no explicit ordering constraint beyond no opposing longs.
Alternative impact scenario (cap reduction) lacks an explicit actor/authorization and timing relative to existing orders beyond the setDivergenceCap call.
